title: How the ER Became the New Doctor's Office — TikTok
notes: Hook question: why do millions of Americans end up in the hospital for something a regular doctor could have caught? Answer, built scene by scene: it tracks where you live and what you earn (map, states, income), then access, then a system that is paid for the fall and not the check-up, and what reverses it (Medicaid expansion, paying for prevention).
All figures are from the article (Oct 7, 2026) and the sources it cites (AHRQ, CMS, KFF, HCCI, MedPAC).

post.headline: How the ER became America's doctor's office
post.caption: Every year 3.5 million adults are hospitalized for something a regular doctor could have caught. Americans in the poorest neighborhoods are 2.5 times more likely to end up there, and an ER visit costs 12 times more than a doctor's office.
post.cta: Full story and interactive maps at the link in bio.

headline.text: {3.5 million} hospital stays a year could have been prevented.

say: Every year, 3.5 million adults are hospitalized for preventable reasons.

scenes.source: How the ER Became the New Doctor's Office · American Inequality
say: Two-thirds of ER visits by privately insured Americans aren't actual emergencies.
We found these numbers are really a map of who lacks access to care.
That map is darkest across Appalachia and the South, and in Mingo County, West Virginia, 1 in 10 hospital stays was preventable.

scenes.title: Preventable hospitalizations per 100,000 Medicare enrollees
say: Across state lines the gap is just as stark, with West Virginia's rate almost three times Hawaii's.

scenes.title: Preventable hospital stays
scenes.subtitle: chronic conditions, per 100,000 people, by neighborhood income
say: Income draws the sharpest line, since Americans in the poorest neighborhoods are 2.5 times more likely to have a preventable hospital stay.

scenes.source: How the ER Became the New Doctor's Office · American Inequality
say: Part of this is access, since about 1 in 5 younger adults can't get an appointment or a doctor outside work hours.

scenes.title: Cost of treating a common condition
scenes.source: How the ER Became the New Doctor's Office · American Inequality
say: By the time they reach the ER, a visit for a common condition costs more than $2,000, twelve times a doctor's office.

scenes.title: Average ER facility fee
say: For hospitals that fall is revenue, and from 2009 to 2016 the average ER facility fee nearly doubled, from $452 to $894.

scenes.title: Primary care doctors
scenes.source: How the ER Became the New Doctor's Office · American Inequality
say: Meanwhile the doctors who could prevent it see over 35% of patient visits yet get about 5% of health spending.

items.headline: Michigan Can Ease Doctor Shortage by Raising Pay for Primary Care, Group Says

say: The system pays well for the hospital stay and poorly for the appointment that would have prevented it.

scenes.title: Pneumonia hospitalizations after Medicaid expansion
scenes.source: How the ER Became the New Doctor's Office · American Inequality
say: When states expand Medicaid, preventable hospitalizations fall, and pneumonia stays drop by two-thirds.

scenes.text: Pay for prevention as reliably as {we pay for treatment.}
say: Preventable hospitalizations will fall when the system pays for prevention as reliably as it pays for treatment.
You can read the full story on American Inequality.
